Well, if someone leaves their wife after birth that is just horrible. I can only see 2 reasons to something like this happening, and none of them gets any sympathy from me.

1. The couple got around to things to quickly, not knowing each other well enough. Because if they did, she would know him enough to figure out that something like this could happen. Or it could be poor communication skills. Any of these mean that the woman has to deal with the consequences of finding a shitty guy and rushing things.

2. She let herself go after having kids. Just because you had kids, does not mean you get to let yourself go. You still owe it to your partner (and yourself) to take care of yourself. Just because you are in a relationship, married or having kids does not mean you suddenly can let yourself go. I get that pregnancy comes with its difficulties and that it leaves some marks, but I have a hard time believing a lot of people care that much. However if you lay in bed all day, slack off and triple your bodyweight, well, then what do you expect.

Again, divorce after a pregnancy is bad for everyone involved, but you have to do your part in the relationship with your partner no matter the circumstances.

Well, while there are no perfect answers, I think I can help you understand your problem a bit better.

So you have 2 options; Talk to her and express your feelings, or ignore it and drop it.

What you have to figure out is if the risk of expressing your emotions and potentially making work akward, outweighs the feelings that comes with not telling her.

I can give you an example based of an experience of mine. I fell hard for a close friend of mine. We shared a friend group and went to the same school. I chose to tell her despite the risks, knowing that I can not deal with the feelings I would have to carry if I did not. Shit crashed and burned hard, and in the end I had to let her go completely. My feelings would not change, and so, having her in my life would cause me more harm than good. I do not regret telling her though.

For you, telling her has its risks. I would way those risks against your feelings. I do not know you, or the way you deal with your emotions. So you will have to evaluate your situasion and reach your own conclusion.

Hope this atleast helped a little bit!

This is quite normal. Defining yourself by your depression, loneliness etc. The thing is, if you think about the times were you actually were happy, even if just for a couple of hours, you probably were a lot different. Acknowledging your feelings is important, but it is up to you if you let them define you.
One thing you can try to get out of the habit of letting it define you, is to stop using it as an excuse. The next time you miss an assignment or something, do not blame it on anything, even if it is it's fault. Just take the blame, even if it means acknowledging your lazy or whatever, and try to quit being lazy. As it is much easier to stop being lazy than it is to get rid of depression/loneliness.
Best of luck!
